analysis.body:
# Interconnection Queue Snapshot: September 2026

Across the five major US grid operators, nearly 9,500 generation and storage projects totaling 1.33 million megawatts sit in interconnection queues awaiting network studies, approvals, or construction completion. ERCOT leads with 438,000 MW from 1,778 projects; NYISO follows with 319,000 MW from 1,414 projects. These queued resources far exceed today's installed capacity, reflecting years of accumulated requests. The composition varies by region: ERCOT's queue is dominated by solar (150,000 MW) and storage (160,000 MW), while gas remains substantial (78,000 MW); MISO's 3,833 projects are also solar-heavy at 145,000 MW, and SPP similarly shows solar and wind leadership. Storage now appears as a major queue category across all operators—160,000 MW in ERCOT alone—signaling grid operators' recognition that intermittent renewable capacity requires buffering.

Commercial-sector electricity sales across eight key states totaled 54,798 gigawatt-hours for the period ending June 2026, with prices ranging from a low of $8.66 per MWh in Texas to a high of $27.33 in California. Texas dominates the volume with 15,754 GWh of commercial sales, followed by California at 10,025 GWh and Georgia at 5,547 GWh. These figures capture data center loads as part of the broader commercial class; they do not isolate data center demand but track the same underlying trends. High-price states like California and Virginia, which reported $27.33 and $10.99 per MWh respectively, represent regions where queued capacity growth is most constrained relative to demand, whereas Texas's lower price reflects relative generation abundance despite its large queue.

Watch whether storage projects in ERCOT, CAISO, and SPP queues move from study phase to construction within the next six months, as their pace of deployment will signal how quickly operators can co-locate battery capacity with solar and wind additions to support sustained data center load.
